editions.title: Legal AI's first listing talk is a contract question for buyers
editions.standfirst: Harvey has sounded out its regular law firm advisers on a listing, and buyers of legal AI now have a supplier-stability question to put in writing.

editions.title: A&O Shearman's $1.1bn AI plan is mostly lawyers' time
editions.standfirst: A&O Shearman puts $1.1bn on a five-year AI strategy, and the firm says most of it is lawyers' time.

editions.title: Courts will not cut a bill on AI alone
editions.standfirst: The US Tenth Circuit upheld a $114,663.11 fee award to Brownstein Hyatt Farber Schreck, so a challenge to a bill on AI grounds needs specific entries behind it.

editions.title: Weil's data has bidders, but no buyer yet
editions.standfirst: Scissero, Crosby and Vetta want pieces of Weil, Gotshal & Manges, and who may sell a collapsing firm's client data is now a live question.

editions.title: The NCSC's AI warning is really about cheap technology
editions.standfirst: The National Cyber Security Centre says UK critical national infrastructure faces AI-powered attacks within two years, and puts the blame on 'tech on the cheap'.

editions.title: Maine's bar moves to Clio Library: free for members, terms with Clio undisclosed
editions.standfirst: LawSites and LawNext report that the Maine bar switched from Decisis to Clio Library on 1 October, free to members and saving the bar more than $50,000 a year; what Clio gets in return is not disclosed.

editions.title: Legal AI platforms widen their range faster than the evidence
editions.standfirst: Harvey has acquired the sales execution company Aida, its fifth purchase of 2026, Harvey announced on 29 October; no price or terms are given.

editions.title: Harvey keeps buying, and buyers should read their contracts
editions.standfirst: Harvey's purchase of Aida, its fifth deal this year, shows how quickly the ownership of a legal AI supplier can change.

editions.title: Weil's troubles are being blamed on AI without evidence
editions.standfirst: Weil, Gotshal and Manges says its management committee has recommended an orderly wind-down, with a partner vote expected within days, and the AI explanations on offer are running ahead of the facts.

editions.title: Hidden AI labels on human-written documents deserve a buyer's attention
editions.standfirst: Greg Lambert reports that Lexis Protégé tags typed Word files as AI-generated, and says a week passed without a public vendor statement.

editions.title: Clio widens its platform; firms may have to prove AI control
editions.standfirst: Clio's purchase of a regulatory monitoring company, announced by Clio itself, extends a practice management platform into compliance territory, with price and terms unstated.

editions.title: AML compliance improves, on the regulator's own evidence
editions.standfirst: The Solicitors Regulation Authority says fewer firms are failing anti-money laundering rules, but "partially compliant" carries most of the good news and its definition is loose.

editions.title: Mary Technology's fact tools arrive in Harvey by connector, with the price still unstated
editions.standfirst: Mary Technology has announced a connector that brings its fact-investigation tools into Harvey; the release says what they do but not what they cost or which firms get them.

editions.title: Courts set the AI timetable; vendors supply the numbers
editions.standfirst: A near five-hour hearing in Concord Music v. Anthropic leaves more to come on 30 October, while Everlaw and 8am offer figures that have yet to meet a second source.

editions.title: A federal judge loses a case over AI errors
editions.standfirst: The Fifth Circuit has taken a judge off a case over AI-linked errors in his orders, and the opinion is now public.

editions.title: Legora's $8.8bn price tag is a bet, not a result
editions.standfirst: Legora's $550m raise at an $8.8bn valuation raises the stakes for legal AI platforms, and the company says Atreides led.

editions.title: AI is not a legal entity, so the solicitor stays accountable
editions.standfirst: The Law Society of England and Wales has reminded solicitors that AI is not a legal entity, which leaves responsibility for its output where it already sat.

editions.title: Research content is moving into the AI platforms, with claims attached
editions.standfirst: Midpage says its research costs a tenth of Westlaw and Lexis and now feeds Harvey; the price claim is a spokesperson's and no pricing is given.

editions.title: The gap at the top of UK law is widening
editions.standfirst: PwC's annual law firm survey, reported by Legal Futures, finds the top 100 firms still growing while the gap between the top 10 and the rest widens.

editions.title: Paying law firms for their emails puts privilege on the table
editions.standfirst: Above the Law reports that a technology company is paying law firms for access to their emails, and client privilege is the stake.

editions.title: Microsoft arrives in legal through the door lawyers already use
editions.standfirst: Microsoft has launched Copilot for Legal, according to Artificial Lawyer, and the stake is who owns the lawyer's desktop.

editions.title: Freshfields reportedly eyes outside capital for its AI unit
editions.standfirst: Legal Business, citing the Financial Times, reports that Freshfields is weighing external investment in its AI unit, and the stake is who ends up owning the tools a firm's lawyers rely on.

editions.title: Two legal AI rivals launch Intake; the name is the lesser point
editions.standfirst: Legora and Harvey each unveiled a product called Intake within a day of one another, and the buyer's question is what each does with the work it routes.

editions.title: The SRA asks what AI means for solicitor competence
editions.standfirst: The SRA has opened an eight week consultation on how technology and AI should shape solicitors' learning and development, with the Statement of Solicitor Competence in scope.
